bottom_line: The Biden-era BIS AI Diffusion Rule — a global three-tier export control regime for advanced AI chips and model weights — was rescinded by the Trump administration two days before its enforcement deadline (May 13 vs. May 15, 2025). A replacement rule is pending; compliance posture for Tier 2 countries (India, UAE, Singapore, Israel and ~140 others) remains undefined.
what_changed: BIS published an Interim Final Rule on January 15, 2025 establishing tiered global licensing requirements for exports of advanced AI chips (3A090.a threshold: H100-class and above) and closed-weight AI model weights trained above 10^26 FLOP. Countries were divided into Tier 1 (18 allies, unrestricted), Tier 2 (~140 countries, compute caps and datacenter authorization requirements), and Tier 3 (China, Russia, Iran and embargoed states, effective ban). The rule never reached its May 15, 2025 enforcement date: on May 13, 2025, BIS announced rescission and promised a replacement within 4-6 weeks.
why_it_matters: Export compliance functions, cloud providers, chip manufacturers, and data center operators had begun structuring operations around the tier framework. Rescission does not restore the pre-rule baseline — it creates a gap in which the prior China-specific controls remain in force but the global tier architecture is undefined. Companies that built Tier 2 expansion plans now face regulatory uncertainty until a replacement rule is published.
affected_actors: advanced AI chip exporters (NVIDIA, AMD, Intel)
cloud providers with global data center footprints
Tier 2 country customers and data center operators (India, UAE, Singapore, Israel, Saudi Arabia)
export compliance and trade counsel at technology companies
investors in AI infrastructure in Tier 2 markets
main_uncertainty: Scope and timeline of the replacement rule: whether it will replicate the global tier architecture, revert to China-specific controls only, or introduce a new structure. BIS gave a 4-6 week estimate in May 2025; no replacement has been published as of the analysis date.

scenarios.name: China-specific revert
scenarios.description: Replacement rule narrows scope back to China, Macau, and embargoed states. Tier 2 countries regain unrestricted access. Industry lobbying (SIA) and administration's stated competitiveness rationale make this plausible.
indicators: Federal Register IFR limiting ECCN 3A090.a controls to EAR Country Group D:5
BIS statements removing per-country compute caps for non-D:5 countries
SIA endorsement of replacement rule language

scenarios.name: Modified global tier structure
scenarios.description: Replacement rule retains a tiered global architecture but with higher compute thresholds, larger country caps, or expanded Tier 1 list. Compliance burden reduced but not eliminated for Tier 2.
indicators: Federal Register IFR retaining per-country cap language with revised thresholds
BIS datacenter authorization program maintained with lighter requirements
Tier 1 expansion to include UAE, Saudi Arabia, or India

SIA and ITI formal responses to replacement rule
